skill.name: firecrawl-download
skill.description: Download a website or selected sections into local Firecrawl files. Use it for offline documentation, screenshots, links, and page archives.
skill.summary: Save website pages locally with Firecrawl formats, filters, screenshots, and organized output.
skill.author: firecrawl

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, example.com URLs, and relative documentation links. The remaining risks are contextual: the skill permits unpinned npx execution and encourages skipping confirmation for bulk downloads.

remediation.suggestion: Require a trusted installed Firecrawl CLI or pin the package version before allowing npx execution.

remediation.issue: Confirmation prompt is bypassed by default guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to always pass -y and require explicit user approval for automated or large downloads.

remediation.issue: Bulk downloads can write many untrusted files locally
remediation.suggestion: Recommend limits, include paths, and a dedicated output folder for every automated download.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned NPX Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows Bash(npx firecrawl *), which can resolve and execute an npm package at runtime. This creates supply-chain and version drift risk for a network and filesystem tool.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools entry explicitly permits npx firecrawl commands, and no package version pin is shown. The risk depends on installer behavior, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Confirmation Bypass
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to always pass -y and says to use it in automated flows. This removes a confirmation safeguard before bulk downloads and local file writes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text directly instructs use of -y to skip confirmation. The skill also downloads many pages to disk, so the operational impact is clear.

content.value_statement: Saving documentation by hand is slow and easy to miss. This skill uses Firecrawl to map pages, download selected content, and organize local files.
actual_capabilities: Maps a website before downloading discovered pages.
Saves downloaded pages under a local .firecrawl directory.
Exports Markdown, links, screenshots, or multiple formats per page.
Filters downloads with search, include paths, exclude paths, and page limits.
Supports scrape options such as main content extraction, wait settings, countries, and languages.
limitations: Requires the Firecrawl CLI and any required Firecrawl configuration.
Can only download content that Firecrawl can access from the target site.
Large sites can take time and use significant local storage.
Does not verify copyright, license, or permission to archive a site.

use_cases.title: Build Offline Documentation Sets
use_cases.description: Download product or API docs as local Markdown files for review without constant network access.

use_cases.title: Archive Web Research Sources
use_cases.description: Save selected pages, links, and screenshots from a source site for later analysis.

use_cases.title: Capture Site Sections for QA
use_cases.description: Download specific paths with screenshots to compare content, links, and page structure.

prompt_templates.title: Download a Small Documentation Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Download [URL] as Markdown for offline reading. Limit the run to 20 pages and ask before any larger download.

prompt_templates.title: Save Pages With Screenshots
prompt_templates.prompt: Download [URL] with Markdown and screenshots. Include only the docs section and keep the saved files organized.

prompt_templates.title: Filter a Site Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Download [URL] with Markdown and links. Include /guides and /api, exclude translated paths, and set a practical page limit.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Review Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a local review snapshot of [URL]. Save main content, links, and screenshots, then summarize what was downloaded and skipped.

output_examples.input: Download the product docs for offline review.
output_examples.output: A local .firecrawl folder contains organized Markdown pages and a short summary of the downloaded documentation URLs.
Each saved guide page includes readable content and a screenshot, grouped by the site path.

output_examples.input: Archive only API pages and skip translations.
output_examples.output: Only matching API pages are saved, translated sections are excluded, and the run reports page counts.

best_practices: Set page limits and include paths before downloading large sites.
Confirm that the target site allows automated downloading.
Review saved files before sharing, indexing, or committing them.
anti_patterns: Running unrestricted downloads against an entire production domain.
Using -y in automation without a clear allowlist and page limit.
Downloading authenticated or private pages into shared folders.

faq.question: What does this skill download?
faq.answer: It downloads discovered pages from a target site as local files, such as Markdown, links, and screenshots.

faq.question: Where are the files saved?
faq.answer: The skill describes saving output under a local .firecrawl directory with nested folders by page.

faq.question: Can it limit the download scope?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports limits, search filters, include paths, exclude paths, and subdomain control.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented options include standard screenshots and full page screenshots.

faq.question: Does it require Firecrawl?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires access to the Firecrawl CLI and any credentials or configuration needed by that tool.

faq.question: Is it safe for private websites?
faq.answer: Use caution. Confirm permission first, limit the scope, and keep downloaded private content out of shared folders.
